title: Underwriting Rule on Multiple Protection Plans Held on One Account
content:
Protection is written over a holding, so a household under Pass and Trip Protection that wants its passes,
its lodging and its lessons covered holds a plan for each.

1. **How many plans one account may carry.** The account may carry several plans at once up to the number
   this charter allows, which is 3, counting plans standing as a quote, in force, with a claim open, with a
   claim settled, and stopped for non-payment.
2. **One plan to one holding.** No two live plans are ever written over the same covered holding. Where a
   household asks for more cover on a holding they have already protected, the plan they hold is moved up
   rather than a second one written, because two plans over one holding would pay twice for one loss.
3. **Household cover.** A plan that carries family cover stands for the whole household on the holdings it
   names, and no separate plan is written for a dependant already covered by it.

**The check before a plan is written.** Whether a live plan already stands over the holding is answered from
the collective's own plan records before the plan is quoted, matching on the holding the plan would be written
over together with the season, and counting a plan as live where it stands as a quote, in force, with a claim
open, with a claim settled, or stopped for non-payment. A plan standing given up, expired or closed off is not
live and does not occupy the holding.

**Worked illustrations (hypothetical).** A household holding a plan over a pass, a plan over a residence and a
plan over a lesson enrolment carries 3 plans, which is the number this charter allows; a fourth plan over a
rental agreement would carry the account past it. A household holding one plan over a pass, that plan standing
with a claim settled, has a live plan over that pass, so a second plan over the same pass is not written and
the plan they hold is moved up instead. A household whose only protection plan over a pass stands given up has
no live plan over it, and that pass is free to be covered afresh.
